THIS WPHC IS FILED UNDER ARTICLE 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA, PRAYING TO SET ASIDE/
QUASH THE DETENTION ORDER NO.21/CRM(4)/ DTN/2022
IS PRODUCED AS ANNEXURE-A) ISSUE A WRIT IN THE NATURE OF HABEAS CORPUS DIRECTING THE RESPONDENT NO.3 TO RELEASE THE DETENUE MEHRAJ KHAN.

THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
ALOK ARADHE J., MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
In this writ petition, the petitioner has assailed the validity of the order of detention dated 09.11.2022 and to release the detenue namely Meharaj Khan.
2. Facts giving rise to filing of this appeal briefly stated are that the petitioner is the sister of the detenue.
The detenue is an accused in ten various criminal cases.
The detenue is also 'A' category rowdy sheeter.
The detenue had developed a habit of absconding after commission of offence to avoid his arrest and trial and by his activities, had caused apprehension in the minds of public in general.

Thereupon, an order of detention was passed under Section 3(1) of the Karnataka Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Drug Offenders, Gamblers, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Slum Grabbers and Video or Audio Pirates Act, 1985 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') and the detenue was taken in custody.

The order of detention was forwarded to the State Government for approval on 18.11.2022.
The detenue submitted a representation on 24.11.2022.
The representation submitted by the detenue was rejected by an order dated 06.12.2022.
Thereafter, by an order dated 07.12.2022, order of detention of the detenue was confirmed.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the failure to mention the documents underneath each of the grounds of detention is contrary to the directions issued by the Division Bench of this Court in SMT.JAYAMMA Vs. COMMISSIONER OF POLICE, BENGALURU1.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the detenue was not informed about the timeline for submission of his representation which is in contravention of order dated 26.09.2018 passed in WPHC No.76/2018 in ILR 2019 KAR 1543 SURESH SHETTY Vs. STATE OF KARNATAKA.

sentences.text: It is also urged that the activities of the detenue at the most amounts to law and order problem and not public order and therefore, the Detaining Authority grossly erred in passing an order of detention.

In support of his submissions, he has placed reliance on the decision of Supreme Court in K.K.SARVANA BABU Vs.
STATE OF TAMIL NADU2.
5.

STATE OF TAMIL NADU2

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned State Public Prosecutor-1 has supported the order passed by the respondents and has submitted that on the basis of material produced before the Detaining Authority, it has recorded a subjective satisfaction that it is necessary to detain the detenue under the provisions of the Act.
It is further submitted that no case for interference of the order passed by the Detaining Authority has been made out.
We have considered the submissions made on both sides and have perused the record placed before us.

The Supreme Court in ABDUL GHANI Vs. STATE OF JAMMU AND KASHMIR 3, in paragraph 6, has held as under:
"6.

entities.text: ABDUL GHANI Vs. STATE OF JAMMU AND KASHMIR
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The fourth point urged was that the District Magistrate, when making the order for detention, did not apply his mind, because his order does not mention the existence of any materials which could have impelled him to make the order of detention of the petitioner.
In the order made under Section 3 of the Act, the existence of material does not require to be mentioned.

The order recites that the District Magistrate is satisfied that it is necessary to detain the petitioner with a view to preventing him from acting in a manner prejudicial to the security of the State.

That this satisfaction was based on materials is further clarified by the order of the Government confirming the detention which mentions that the District AIR 1971 SC 1217 Magistrate had, with his report, sent to the Government the grounds on which the order had been made as well as other particulars having bearing on the matter.
It is, therefore, not a case where the District Magistrate can be held to have passed an order without any material at all."

sentences.text: Thus, from the aforesaid enunciation of law, it is evident that in an order of detention, existence of material is not required to be mentioned.
Therefore, the contention of the petitioner that underneath each of the grounds of detention, the documents of which reliance has been placed have not been mentioned, does not deserve acceptance.
Admittedly, in the instant case, order of detention was passed on 09.11.2022.
The detenue was informed about his right to make a representation.
The detenue submitted a representation on 24.11.2022 which has been rejected on 06.12.2022.
The law does not contemplate that no timeline has been mentioned for making such a representation.
Even assuming that such a requirement exists, no prejudice has been caused to the detenue as he has admittedly made a representation which has been considered and rejected.

The Detaining Authority,
on the basis of material placed before it, has recorded a subjective satisfaction which reads as under:
"On observing your activities, it's found that you have a person repeatedly indulging in anti-social activities.
You have a tendency to disturb the peace and public tranquility by indulging in illegal and anti social activities.
You have created a situation of fear in the society by your anti-social activities.
Besides, you are also threatening the witness not to depose their evidence before the court in which you are facing trial.
There is possibility that you will take the law into your hands, and indulge in activities like assaulting the general public for extortion.

Though, you were arrested and remanded to judicial custody in many cases, you have not reformed yourself and still continue to terrorize the public and disturb peace and public order, shows your incorrigible criminal conduct.

From the above, it is clear that if you are allowed to remain free / released on bail you will continue to defeat the normal criminal justice system procedures and indulge in criminal activities like Assault, Attempt to murder, Extortion, Criminal intimidation, etc and creating fear in the minds of people.
Further, your are a threat to public order and peace in the society.

Hence, as you are not amenable under ordinary laws of the land, with a view to prevent you from acting in any manner prejudicial to the maintenance of the public order, I am satisfied that it is absolutely necessary to detain you under the Goonda Act.

I have examined the reports and the material placed before me by the Police Inspector, CCB, through Assistant Commissioner of Police, CCB, OCW and the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Crime-II Bengaluru City.
On perusal of all the material placed before me, it is evident that your criminal activities have caused breach - 10 - of public order and cannot be prevented under ordinary laws of the land.
You have repeatedly violated the bail conditions imposed on you by the Hon'ble Courts.
Your goonda activities are disturbing public tranquility and normal life.

Because of this,
public order is adversely affected and a sense of fear is created in certain parts of Bengaluru City.

sentences.text: 4 In view of the aforesaid grounds, I am convinced that your are a goonda & drug peddler as defined under Section 2 (g) & (e) of the Karnataka Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Drug Offenders, Gamblers, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Slum Grabbers and Video or Audio Pirates Act 1985 (Karnataka Act No.12 of 1985) and that you are likely to indulge in anti-social activities and such other activities prejudicial to the maintenance of public order."

sentences.text: 8. The aforesaid subjective satisfaction is based on material produced before the Detaining Authority.
It - 11 - has come to a conclusion that the activities of the detenue are prejudice to the maintenance of the public order.
The aforesaid subjective satisfaction has been recorded from the basis of the material and the records produced before the Detaining Authority.
Therefore, the contention of the detenue that his activities only pertain to law and order and not public order, does not deserve acceptance.
For the aforementioned reasons, we do not find any merit in the petition.
The same fails and is hereby dismissed.
